target.title: fix(codex): preserve subagent completions after sessions_yield
target.body:
Closes #104806

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a parent session using the Codex runtime could lose a subagent completion after calling `sessions_yield`. The completion wake could be accepted by the old turn immediately before OpenClaw interrupted that turn; Codex then discarded the accepted-but-unconsumed input, while OpenClaw had already treated it as delivered.

This was silent in affected releases: the child task was `completed`, but its result never reached the parent transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

The key protocol distinction is **accepted is not consumed**. `turn/steer` acknowledges after putting input in Codex's pending-input queue. A later `turn/interrupt` clears that queue. Codex separately emits a completed `userMessage` item after it persists and consumes the input.

This change therefore:

- keeps each logical steer pending after the `turn/steer` response and completes it only when the corresponding `userMessage` completion arrives;
- handles both valid wire orders (`steer response → userMessage` and `userMessage → steer response`), ignores the initial turn prompt, and preserves batch/FIFO ordering;
- pauses and cancels pending steering as soon as `sessions_yield` begins terminal release, so the existing announce fallback can retry on a fresh parent turn;
- resumes steering if `sessions_yield` fails or the dynamic-tool batch proves non-terminal; and
- reports a successful yield as `yielded: true`, `livenessState: "paused"`, `stopReason: "end_turn"` so nested Codex orchestrators remain wakeable.

The change is confined to the Codex extension. It does not change shared announce routing, retry policy, or configuration.

The dependency behavior was checked directly against OpenAI Codex at `9121132c8f54`: [`steer_input` queues pending input and returns](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9121132c8f5412ae99c36363409759baa7e004f9/codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs#L2976-L3031), [consumption persists it before emitting the `userMessage` lifecycle](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9121132c8f5412ae99c36363409759baa7e004f9/codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs#L2923-L2937), and [interrupt clears pending state](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9121132c8f5412ae99c36363409759baa7e004f9/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs#L475-L505).

## User Impact

Subagent completions are no longer falsely reported as delivered into a turn that is about to be interrupted. The existing requester-agent handoff can recover them on a fresh turn, and yielded nested Codex orchestrators stay paused until their descendants settle.

No new setting or migration is required. This PR does not reduce the existing announce retry/backoff latency; it prevents silent loss.

## Evidence

### Minimal in-repo reproducer (no gateway or custom harness)

The regression test models the three relevant protocol events: `turn/steer` succeeds, no `userMessage` consumption event arrives, then terminal release cancels the queue.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-steering.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 \
  -t "rejects an acknowledged but unconsumed steer"
```

On current `origin/main` (`5f9a6ce7eb`), adding only that test fails deterministically:

```text
AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
Tests  1 failed | 5 skipped
```

On this branch:

```text
Tests  1 passed | 11 skipped
```

The test is intentionally queue-level so reviewers can reproduce the bug in about four seconds without credentials, a model, a gateway, or the reporter's real-gateway harness.

### Focused validation

```text
attempt-steering.test.ts          12/12 passed
run-attempt.steering.test.ts       9/9 passed
oxfmt                              clean (4 changed files)
oxlint                             clean (4 changed files)
tsc --noEmit -p extensions/codex/tsconfig.json
                                    passed
structured local review            clean
structured branch-vs-main review   clean
```

The lifecycle suite includes the full race in the opposite ordering too: an acknowledged completion wake remains unresolved, `sessions_yield` starts, the queue rejects the wake, and `turn/interrupt` follows. It also covers delayed batches, in-flight requests, failed yields, mixed terminal/non-terminal dynamic-tool batches, initial-prompt disambiguation, prompt answers, and yielded lifecycle metadata.

### Redacted live observation

The original released-build evidence is in #104806 (3/3 on `2026.7.1-beta.5`, 2/2 on `2026.6.11`). A later `main` run recovered through its retry path roughly 23 seconds after child completion; this branch recovered through the same fallback in roughly 22 seconds. That live run supports end-to-end delivery, while the deterministic test above isolates the permanent-loss race and is the primary regression proof.
